responses: I have a letter here for you.
Toodles!
If I must, as they say, "pull out all the stops," then so be it. Behold, my greatest creation!
If I must, as they say, "pull out all the stops," then so be it. Behold, my greatest creation!
Found you, I did! Haha! Numinar says he wants someone, Llavados finds them, and here you are!
Heroes, always wandering around, easy to find! Good thing, because she's in danger!
Who does it matter, what does it matter? You're a hero! You look the type.
It's what you do! Someone's in danger, all my friends are in danger... will be in danger. Whichever.
You find the danger, you stop the danger, you get treasure, simple, easy! Not really though, someone always wants you to fetch something random.
Yes! No. Maybe. Hard to explain, not my area, too Broken, too many mechanisms mostly unmoving! Can take you down, though, introduce you to the team!
Let them explain, they love explaining!
To? Not to, Down! Deep Down! Low as you can go! Can't expect a Chronographer to operate any other way, can you? Have to go down, no other way.
Could use a gate, but... I broke that! Hahaha!
No, your way is Stonehole Mine, nice place, has a contingency! It's right there on your little map! Very nice map too!
But I talk too much! Go to Stonehole Mine, go deep, find the way to our little town! Take me with you!
Follow? No, take me with you!
What you see isn't what I am! Let me shut down, you take what glows from this husk, take me deep down, and we'll see where that leads us!
Yes, perfect! Not really. Not from me. Just take the part that glows, you'll see!
Normally, outsider, I'd throw you off the edge of Lull-Mor, but you returned with Llavados, so I'll give you a chance.
As much as I'm wary of Llavados' schemes, we are a bit desperate down here.
He's Broken. His mind is damaged in a way I don't fully understand. Mad though he may be, he has insights that sometimes help us, sometimes harm us.
He brings things, people, and it is usually a fifty percent chance that it turns out bad for us.
So, that's the chance I'll give. I have with me an old Septim, a coin, tarnished on one side, much like your empire outside.
I will flip it, and if it lands on the unsullied side, you may stay. Otherwise, you will find your home in the equations below.
(Numinar flips the coin)
Seems Sotha Sil smiles on you today, outsider. Let us hope he does the same for us. Now, speak freely, outlander, or go away.
I can see his logic, however twisted. But he didn't tell you what was the problem, did he?
That's not his style. He's not good with words. Or speaking, or handling machinery. He broke the Upgate on his way out, for one thing.
I am better at explaining, so let me try.
We are Chronographers, fabricant servants of the god Seht. We monitor time and space and stop it from collapsing in on itself.
One of the ways we do so is by overseeing the Towers. This particular Tower that we sit under is Snow-Throat, known as the Throat of the World.
But it is malfunctioning.
The towers are one of the most essential mechanisms of the world, the pinpoints of the Wheels of Lull, yet one by one, they are slowly dying.
For years, we have watched the most essential pieces of Snow-Throat, but now it starts to flicker and fade, and we don't know why.
If Snow-Throat has been deactivated or is at risk of such, it is a serious threat, not just to our order, but to Nirn as a whole.
(The FRF gives you a note and a teleport ball, then trundles off.)
But we do not know who or what causes such trouble. We do however, suspect outside forces.
Because you outsiders must always prod that which should not be prod! We are fabricants. We are raised and born to love the machine, to respect it.
But you people pick away at it, and look around with�a sad face when the machine breaks down, and we are the ones that must fix it.
There is no doubt that someone above us�seeks to get at Snow-Throat, or is trying.
But there are enough possible parties that we cannot leave such a thing to guesswork. We must conduct research. We must scout, as it were.
This is precisely what I was thinking.
It is, I admit, hard for us to work on the surface. With our machine-parts and our glowing eyes, we certainly stand out, no? You, however, do not.
People would ignore your presence, and you could operate relatively unmolested.
There are three possible candidates in Skyrim with the ability to affect Snow-Throat, unintentionally or not.
The Greybeards, with their proximity, the College of Winterhold, with its lack of discipline, and the Thalmor, with their meddling.
Near each of their places of residence there will be slotpoints, folds in the world mechanism that can be read for data.
We have this. It is a device that must be installed in these slotpoints, from which it collects what we need.
Installing it is a complicated procedure, requiring use of an Artophysical Manipulator, that is, this tool.
It is not a hammer. It is an Artophysical Manipulator, a very delicate device that simply looks like a hammer!
But using that... tool, it is not the difficult part. It is finding the slots.
The world mechanism's pieces are not able to be located by normal sight.
One must have this device, a visor that, when worn, reveals pieces of the world mechanism for one to manipulate.
Yes, for all three locations, mind you. It is what we call association triangulation.
The three pegs will use all the data collected to tell us just who is messing with our Tower, and where from.
I will warn you though, the pegs are a bit... ornery. Hopefully you will be able to handle yourself. You did after all, reach here.
Speaking of which, use the main elevator from now on. It will make things easier.
If you have further questions, then ask them quickly.
Are you still here? Even Llavados does a better job at his assigned tasks than you!
No, absolutely not! I refuse! I refuse! No way!
Oh, of course they didn't tell you about me! I am the Analyst, intelligence that runs all data collection in Sotha Sil!
Or I was, now relegated to a bunch of pegs and forced to be hit with a hammer whenever a bunch of exiles want something!
Exactly! It's indignifying, it is! If you know them, tell them there's no chance. I won't do it!
Do you think I am so low as to accept a bribe? Well, you are absolutely correct!
I once had a collection of data modules that sparkled like the false sun of the City.
I may not be able to get such things back, but if you brought me something similar - a diamond, perhaps - I would reconsider.
Then let it be known I am an intelligence of my word. I will collect your data with that diamond. A paltry module for a paltry task!
Perhaps you have, but I will not know if you did it correctly until I receive notification from the intelligence itself.
(A tone sounds from somewhere on Numinar.)
Numinar, you slave-driving fool, if you needed someone to tell you the Thalmor were up to no good, you didn't need to contact me!
Next time you want the obvious relayed to you, go talk to a child!
Wait, the Thalmor are messing with the World Mechanisms?
Maybe not all of them, I'm not one for bigotry, but some yellow-skin up on Whitehorn Pass is certainly looking into it, it seems!
Bunch of bananas can't leave well enough alone, can they? Erasing Lorkhan, and now going after the Throat of the World!
I suppose it was obvious that the Thalmor were trying to interfere with our work, but I still needed to hear it from the Analyst.
Pyandonean fruit. It's long, yellow, and smells. Like the Thalmor.
At any rate, I will need to meditate on this information. Feel free to look around until then. I'm sure you have some task you consider worthwhile.
Yes, but no. The Thalmor simply being involved in something is inevitable. Them trying to destroy the world is highly expected.
We need specifics. We need to know who, why, how. I do not like crawling around blindly. I am a fabricant, and I demand information!
I prefer the word infiltrate. We now know where whatever bit of the Thalmor responsible are located. It would be simple enough to storm the place.
No. Delicate, that's the key here. Stumbling blindly is not our way.
We don't know who is involved or what, hence the infiltrating.
Instead of a full-out assault, I'm going to send an agent in, disguised as one of their number.
They go in, they retrieve what information they can, and get out. Simple, easy, and efficient.
Precisely. You have better knowledge of surface world social cues than we do.
Also, you can eat normal food without exploding, and the Thalmor do love their feasts and parties.
We managed to scavenge these robes. They'll be enchanted to disguise any... excess details, and you should be able to blend in.
With a few forged documents and some sneaking, you should be just fine.
The place is called Whitehorn Pass. It was an old Imperial outpost on the northern Cyrod border in the second era. Now it belongs to the Thalmor.
This time, however, I don't want you traveling there on foot. Too risky. No, use the Upgate this time. It's about time we give you access to that.
The Upgate. We don't have a helicarrier like a proper chronography team, but it serves its purpose for getting us around.
Head to the building with the big spikes all over it. Talk to Subori there. She'll lay things out for you.
Now understand me, outsider! I have had to deal with breakdowns, bustups and malfunctions on this gate, and it is not something I enjoy doing!
Just because I am the one who cleans up your messes does not mean you are to go around making them.
This is a delicate piece of equipment. You will treat it with the same respect you would any other machine, or I will tan your hide with a chain!
When I was a young girl, I used to work for Pevlar, and he worked a kind of magic on a transport gate. Some of it rubbed off on me, so here I am.
The Upgate is our way of surface travel, much smoother than an elevator, and I can set its destination to just about anywhere we need to go.
Oh, you need to use it now? That's... um...
The last one to use the gate was Llavados. I've no idea where he got a key to this place...
But he ran through half-naked, covered in butter, screaming in a strange language. I'm still working on cleaning up the mess.
When it comes to Llavados and butter, it is always a problem.
He didn't really cover himself in it. It was more like he flooded the entire chamber with it.
Verminous fabricant butter is nasty stuff. Distilled, it makes a good lubricant, but if not, it sticks in machinery and is a pain to clean out!
I managed to get most of it, but there's still some pockets of the stuff in the lower pump mechanisms.
You would actually help me? You don't have ulterior motives, do you, outsider?
Hmm... Very well. I'm not one to look a Khajiit in the mouth when it gives me something. You may help.
The pump mechanisms alternate and move enough that you should be able to scoop out the pockets of butter if you're quick enough.
Don't come crying to me if you lose a limb, though. I'm not reattaching it!
Have you? Well, there is only one way to find out, then, isn't there? Step through the gate when you're ready.
I recommend a running start, though. It hurts less.
I have a much more important task, outsider. I must contact the leader of our order, the Eternity, and requisition both guards and equipment.
And, at any rate, do I even look like I'm the least bit combat-ready?
There were security systems and machines all throughout the Foundry, and while I might not last, you certainly would.
No, the Upgate only goes, as the name suggests, up. The Boiling Foundry is much further down, in the dark places of Sotha Sil below us.
You can't reach it via the Upgate. However, Lull-Mor used to have an elevator station to and from the Foundry.
It was removed long ago, but the current station once led to it. Perhaps, if you are clever, you might find a way in? Maybe see what others can't?
Part of me wonders how you even understood what you were looking for, considering I never described it in the first place.
But as I've said, no point in wondering such things when we've got what we need.
The work teams from the Voidyards have arrived, after quite a bit of deliberating, but I still need time to prepare.
When we finish drilling to the Stone, which may take a while, then I shall contact you again.
In the meantime, feel free to relax and do... whatever it is outsiders do.
You better have that drillbit, outsider. Otherwise, why are you talking to me?
You. Come with me. Now.
There's been a problem.
I never said you did. You are a problem, but not all of my problems. This one is, unfortunately, unrelated to you.
No, but we are very close. It seems I might have miscalculated the route to it. Some of the mining teams are dead, attacked by undead fabricants.
Not as you might understand it. They're constructs for the most part.
It seems that we, on accident, drilled into a previously unknown section of the catacombs of Sotha Sil. But I do not understand what agitates them.
A fabricant, dead or not, understands the need of the machine.
They are our ancestors, and would not attack us unless something was seriously wrong, but once again, we stumble blindly.
If you would be so kind as to, you would have our gratitude. They broke in around the digsite tunnel, so start looking there.
As soon as you clear out those catacombs, we can proceed. Otherwise, why are you talking to me?
Lay still, Dovahkiin. You're not in any danger.
You're... awake, correct? That is the term when someone is not sleeping, yes? Awake?
As I understand Lord Fyr, you fought valiantly against a powerful Unwound.
The fight collapsed the cavern in, but by then, you were too exhausted to escape. He and his compatriot found you and brought you back here.
Yes, that would be me. Hello.
I'm afraid the Lord title is a bit much. I haven't sat on the Telvanni council for years, but the fabricants have always enjoyed their honorifics.
But please, allow me to introduce myself. I am Divayth Fyr, an old friend of Sotha Sil. My friend here is Yagrum Bagarn.
I've not been a dwarf for quite some time, and before that, I was not a dwarf either. So no, I am not a dwarf. I was a dwarf.
However, I am a Dwemer. The last living Dwemer.
I see you know your history. It is good to see they still teach children about me.
But no, Dovahkiin, Yagrum's unfortunate appearance back in the Third Era was due to the disease known as Corprus.
With the demise of Dagoth Ur, the disease receded enough to the point where I could restore Yagrum to what he once was.
Neither me nor Yagrum have figured that out yet. I would watch your back, though.
As funny and quirky as fabricants might seem, they are the children of Sotha Sil, and a rogue fabricant can put up a fight.
Indeed? Well, my warning remains the same then. Watch your back.
I feel honored to have Lord Fyr here. Not for centuries has he visited the Clockwork City.
I have a delayed reaction to these things, remember? Fyr's arrival and the existence of a saboteur may complicate things.
I've got to plan for said complications.
Currently? No. In the future? Maybe.
Fyr can provide adequate protection and allow us to complete the dig, and once at the Stone, he will no doubt be instrumental in defeating Archeron.
Of course not. We still need dumb muscle, and you've proven yourself in that matter already.
It's just that with the undead dealt with, things will be running smoothly enough. I'll contact you once we reach the Cave.
Not well, not well! Saboteur amongst us eh, makes his move and here we go!
Oh, for Seht's sake, get in here, you fool! We're under attack!
So, it's you.
Yes, and yet it's all been to reach the Stone. It's obvious now.
You destroy the only thing keeping us safe. You convince us that our ward is in danger.
You convince us to dig to it, and then you and your Thalmor masters reap the rewards.
I told you that Llavados' little ideas only work half the time. It seems that this time, he was wrong, as was the coin toss. And so was I.
I really thought better of you. Guards, take this Thalmor lackey to the cells!
I am so sorry about this, truly, but you were in the way.
Oh, right.
Now, isn't this familiar. Once again, we're talking through the bars to each other.
Hello! Honestly, what are the chances the one person I disguise myself as is the one person these machines would fawn over?
It's quite interesting, really. As is the fact that our good friend Numinar arrives at the correct conclusion, but for the wrong person.
I had theories, but getting the fabricants to do the heavy work for me was far more convenient.
What can I say, I am an opportunist, and opportunity is awaiting. Goodbye, my friend.
Perhaps you could, but this cell is not a cell, rather an old lift, suspended over what I can only call a bottomless pit. Understand?
Yes, oh. Masscroft, if you would be so kind.
Get up. Please, get up. You are needed.
Good, you're alive. You're hardier than I expected, and I expected much.
It is a facade. Oh, Numinar thinks he knows me, but the gibbering and rambling serves but a purpose. As do you.
I know.
You'd be surprised at the things I know. More than the other Chronographers do. You see, Dovahkiin, I am much more than a simple washermer.
Perhaps someday you may learn who I am, and my real name, and of course, you have already met Memory.
I shall be quick. Memory is the progeny of Seht, Sotha Sil's final creation, a child of mer, machine, and Lullian magic.
Many years from now, there will be a disaster that will destroy the world. You cannot stop it, avoid, or in any way prevent it.
However, with the help of Memory, we can survive it, the people of that time escaping the destruction to build a new life, a new world.
But if Memory is not there, all will be lost.
My cohorts believe the Towers of Nirn only keep reality stable. They are, as always, half-right.
The Towers do not just keep Nirn alive, but Memory as well. She is young, barely above that of an infant, and she cannot survive on her own.
That is my job. I care for her, keep her safe, until she can walk on her own.
But with each tower that falls, Memory has been placed further and further into danger.
If the Justiciar reaches the Stone of Snow Throat, a thing we call The Cave, he will use it, and he will destroy it. And when it dies, so will Memory.
You may not feel the consequences, but your children's children will, as will the rest of the world.
Indeed. But now at least, you understand the true and most pressing need of it.
You cannot kill Archeron.
He has, though rudimentary, an understanding of the Wheels of Lull far beyond that of normal mortals.
He has, shall I say, "hacked" himself into its mechanisms, making himself and his foul experiments all but indestructible by normal means.
So, of course, you will use unusual means.
Here, in these depths, there are many things, including equipment built of the same stuff Archeron uses, that would unwind his windings.
Prove yourself to the Bottom of the World, and you would find yourself granted the power to defeat Archeron once and for all.
Oh, and I might want to watch out for that large fellow, Masscroft. Dying doesn't seem to be something he does easily. Off you go now.
They've all gone up to the Cave. I suggest you do too, if you're looking to catch Archeron, or should I say "Lord Fyr".
I did say I know everything. I would have intervened, of course, but then again, I wouldn't have. Now, do you need anything?
Find the power you need down here, and you may stand a chance to save Memory.
You are a Shezzarine, protecting the world is in your very soul.
Oh, hi.
I think I know that already.
Maybe not a few of the team, but the sudden appearance of his constructs tipped me off. There's also the fact that he's standing behind you.
I am honestly trying to consider what to say to you that wouldn't simply come off as cliche or gloating.
I'd say so, considering I quite literally threw you down a bottomless pit and sent Masscroft after you to make sure.
Given that you're alive, I think it's quite clear that I need to throw you down a deeper pit and send someone much larger after you.
I'll start with this pit, and for the someone, I elect myself!
Oh, well done! And welcome back!
Past the bottom of the world, friend, you fell all the way down. This is the core of Nirn. This was Magnus' workshop.
This was the central mainframe of Sotha Sil. This is Memory's room. And to some extent, mine.
Dead, more than dead.
Poor bastard integrated himself into the mechanisms so much that upon his death, his soul became a part of the machine...
Now he will be splayed out across its gears and equations forevermore. Still, I've seen worse happen, and serves him right.
We have met before, Dragonborn, you don't remember, of course. Let us simply say that I understand what it means to walk in the shoes of a god.
That I owe a favor to an old friend who I left neglected. Let us say that I am as much a godfather to Memory as I am an architect.
Take care, friend, we shall return you back to Lull-Mor to watch over the Tower.
We'll see each other again come Landfall. For now, the Wheels of Lull shall turn unmolested.
You're back! Have you seen Llavados?
Oh. Eh, that happens sometimes. I once went out with a lady who was... well, that's a story for another day. I suppose I owe you an apology.
That's not how we work, outsider. We are chronographers. Problems come, and we fix them and move on. It is our way.
Was the adventure not enough? No, I suppose not, I know how it is. I'm afraid I don't have much to offer you, but maybe in the future.
Avarri might have something for you, that shield of yours certainly interested him.
And uh, you are welcome in Lull-Mor at any time. I suppose defeating an insane Thalmor Mystic earns that honor at least.
I should have simply lobotomized you when I had the chance!
I control the World Mechanism now, no more games!
A shield with a gear on it won't save you!
I am as strong as Sotha Sil was! Do you really think you can defeat me?
Poltergeists, they are, object manipulators. Watch your back!
There we are, the old lift! Well, old on your terms, new on mine! Down we go, down we go, through the Wheels of Lull until we reach the bottom!
Touch anything and I take you apart.
We're watching you... scum.
Go ahead, make my day.
We're just here to defend the place.
Let's not make this official, outsider. Move along.
Like the harquebus? See Avarri, he does good work.
That rifle... It is... nice.
Hey.
I'm busy, but that doesn't mean much to you, does it?
The only thing you need to know about me is that I don't trust you. But I do not trust anyone.
Don't hold it against yourself, though I doubt you're a nice enough person to do so.
There was a time when... never mind. We have our jobs to do around here, and that is what I do.
I suppose you've earned my respect. I was an overclocker, a mechanic, when I was younger. Those were good times, and I was happy then.
But curiosity kills the scrib, and I was very curious. I broke into too many things, studied the wrong things.
Then the city died, and I was shipped out with the rest of the Chronographers. A few more angry superior officers later, and here I am.
I've learned to stop being so curious.
Back, are we?
Like the helmet? I don't. Why am I wearing it?
You've got to protect the things you care about, Dovahkiin.
Normal life, normal me! But broken now, Numinar's assistant all smashed up in his mind!
Oh not on purpose! Don't blame him, it's the way of the fabricant. We gladly experiment on each other and ourselves! Casualties are inevitable!
Caisus? Caisus, is that you? You need to come closer, I can't see like I used to.
It's always dark, you know. I hope that means the end is coming. But I guess the only light at the end of the tunnel is us.
Hope's for men without wheels, isn't it? Isn't it always?
Oh. You... you are not Caisus. Nor are you fabricant. Have you come to kill me?
What a thing to ask! Do you mean who am I? Who was I? I still remember that.
I was a poet you know. Perhaps not a good one, as evident by my locomotivish fate but... Did I deserve this? Did I deserve what they did to me?
The Diolkos! The Resource Men! The tracklayers and factorybuilders and candlemakers!
Speak a word wrong, think a thought the Emperor doesn't like, and they're upon you.
I penned but a single pamphlet for my prince: A list of grievances, and this is the fate the Emperor's great fleshforgers placed me into.
Trust in the Diolkos, we were always told. They will make your lives better, the empire told us.
But how good is your life when they turn your wife into a caboose and your children into belt drivers in a textile mill?
What happens when you realize what they really mean when they tell you that the citizens of the Empire are your greatest resource?
The Diolkos! How can you not know the Diolkos?
Their banners hang in every street, their words fill every tavern, their machines in every house in every city across the empire.
Their factories choke the skies! The rivers run indigo with their bile and runoff! The white moths turn black. You haven't heard of them?
Alessia save me... How long has it been? Did Reman finally see reason? Where have they gone? How can one not know of the great Workmen?
He is... gone? Then...
Some of us, the other engines, hoped for absolution, you know. An end to the sin of the railroad.
Some believed that if they worked hard, that if they were really useful, the Emperor would grant them a final death.
I thought myself the last Wailway engine, that the others had all been scrapped and freed from this hell.
I've sat here in the darkness for so long, screaming into the silence of the cogs...
You, other being. I have a request for you.
Would you please kill me?
I have lost track of time. I have forgotten my own face, my own name.
Every moment I exist is a moment I can feel the bloated steam in this wretched shell pumping through me.
I do not wish to be, and I do not wish to even be less.
I cannot ambulate as you do, other being. But if I could, I would use my mobility to take my own life.
Please, there is little I can offer you, besides the promise that, were our roles reversed, I would do the same. Find a way to end me.
Kill me. Let me die.
I did not think you would return.
The darkness is always there.
Why did the clockmaker bring me here? Why was I forgotten? Am I not useful?
I am a wailway locomotive: a soul bound to an engine of movement, made to pull trains of goods and passengers along the routes of Cyrod.
Ours was a drunken dream of a foolish prince, made into real nightmare by the will of the Diolkos.
The dead bound and eternally enslaved; ever screaming, ever in agony, and ever moving forward to Reman's glorious dawn.
Do you know what it is like to see without eyes? To scream without a mouth?
To have your throat bleed even though you've only fetid water and coal sludge pumping through the pipes that don't even form a throat?
I am always in pain. I will never not be in pain. But I've grown used to it. The boredom is far worse.
My tender. He provided the fuel, I provided the motion. He was...
He was not a good man in life. His crimes deserved horrific punishment. But in the end he suffered the same fate I did, and that made him something t
Not a friend. There are no friends for a locomotive.
When Reman sold me to the dark elven clockmaker, I had assumed that it was merely the precursor to more labor.
But he poked and prodded at me, asked me questions, and then left me here. I sometimes wonder what he wanted with me.
I sometimes wonder if the alternative was better. At least I'd have been outside. At least I'd suffer in company.
Shatter the shell, break the machine, smash the container that imprisons my self.
I do not remember much, but I remember the clockmaker taking my carriages and pieces and studying them.
When he was done, he would dispose of them, smashing them and discarded them like used scraps.
This workshop was used to transport and destroy them. Perhaps the same can be done to me?
